purpose: machine-readable ontology of concrete linguistic-analysis work-units across the structural core of language (phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics) for finding, executing, evaluating, and synthesizing rigorous linguistic analysis.
assumptions: Structural linguistics is modeled as a subdomain of linguistics covering the formal core: phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable linguistic-analysis work-units (methods and decision areas), not topics to read about.
No observed dataset is supplied; all metrics are heuristic priors grounded in standard pedagogy (Fromkin/Rodman/Hyams; Yule).
Analysis proceeds from documented primary data through phonetics to semantics, with cross-module reconciliation before handoff.
exclusions: Sociolinguistics, pragmatics-beyond-reference, and discourse analysis as ends in themselves.
Computational NLP engineering and statistical language modeling as deliverables.

competency_questions.question: Which IPA segments and feature values does a given speech sample contain?
What is the phoneme inventory of the language and which allophones realize each phoneme?
Which ordered phonological rules and prosodic patterns derive surface forms?
How is a word segmented into morphemes and arranged into an inflectional paradigm?
Which word-formation processes are productive in the language?
To which lexical category does each word belong on distributional grounds?
What constituents, phrase-structure rules, and trees describe a sentence's syntax?
Which grammatical relations (subject, object) hold, and on what diagnostics?
How many structural readings does an ambiguous string have and which trees license them?
Is an analysis typologically plausible against cross-linguistic universals?
What are the sense relations of a word and how do parts compose into sentence meaning?
How is the reference of an expression distinguished from and fixed relative to its sense?
Are the phonological, morphological, syntactic, and semantic analyses mutually consistent?
Is the analysis documented reproducibly from primary data with provenance?

glossary.definition: a minimal contrastive sound unit that distinguishes meaning
a context-predictable phonetic variant of a phoneme
a minimal pairing of form and meaning
morphology realizing grammatical features without changing lexical category
morphology forming new lexemes, often changing category or core meaning
a word group that functions as a syntactic unit on diagnostic tests
a syntactic function such as subject or object defined by diagnostics, not meaning
the conventional meaning of an expression versus the entity it picks out
the principle that sentence meaning is a function of part meanings and structure

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from standard structural-linguistics pedagogy and reference works (Fromkin, Rodman & Hyams, An Introduction to Language; Yule, The Study of Language) and analytic practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Render speech as IPA symbols, distinguishing articulatory place, manner, and voicing for each segment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new speech sample or articulatory reanalysis arrives

pros.claim: transcription fixes a stable observational record before any abstraction
pros.example: narrow IPA captures aspiration the spelling hides

cons.claim: narrow transcription over-specifies detail irrelevant to contrast
cons.example: coding every coarticulation effect bloats the record

acceptance_tests: every segment carries place, manner, and voicing

nodes.definition: Establish the phoneme inventory of a language by minimal pairs and complementary distribution of allophones.
contradictors: analyst who treats every phone as contrastive

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when transcription is revised or new contrastive data appears

pros.claim: minimal pairs give an operational test for contrast
pros.example: 'pin' vs 'bin' proves /p/-/b/ contrast

cons.claim: sparse data leaves contrast undecidable
cons.example: a missing minimal pair forces a distributional argument

failure_modes: contrast missed from gaps in data
acceptance_tests: each phoneme supported by a minimal pair or distribution argument
allophones assigned to a parent phoneme

nodes.definition: Write ordered rewrite rules in distinctive features that derive surface allophones from underlying phonemes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the phoneme inventory or alternation data changes

pros.claim: feature rules capture natural classes a list cannot
pros.example: one rule devoices all final obstruents

cons.claim: rule ordering can be indeterminate without enough forms
cons.example: feeding vs bleeding order needs decisive data

acceptance_tests: each rule targets a natural class by features

nodes.definition: Analyze stress, tone, intonation, and syllable structure as suprasegmental organization above the segment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when transcription or pitch annotation is revised

pros.claim: prosody explains contrasts segments miss
pros.example: stress distinguishes 'PERmit' noun from 'perMIT' verb

cons.claim: intonation meaning is gradient and context-bound
cons.example: the same contour can signal question or doubt

failure_modes: lexical stress confused with phrasal stress

nodes.definition: Cut words into morphemes and identify allomorphs by comparing forms across a paradigm.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new word forms or glosses enter the paradigm

pros.claim: paradigm comparison reveals recurrent meaning-form units
pros.example: 'cats'='cat'+'-s' isolates the plural morpheme

cons.claim: portmanteau and zero morphs resist clean cutting
cons.example: French 'au'=a+le fuses two morphemes

acceptance_tests: each cut recurs with stable meaning

nodes.definition: Map the inflectional system of a category by tabulating forms against grammatical features like case, number, and tense.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new inflected forms or features are added

pros.claim: paradigms expose systematic feature-form mappings
pros.example: a Latin noun paradigm crosses case by number

cons.claim: syncretism hides distinct features under one form
cons.example: English present tense marks only 3sg

acceptance_tests: every cell maps features to a form

nodes.definition: Analyze how new lexemes are built by derivation, compounding, and other word-formation processes, with their productivity.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new derived forms or productivity data appear

pros.claim: derivation rules predict possible new words
pros.example: '-ness' productively makes nouns from adjectives

cons.claim: lexicalized forms block rule-based prediction
cons.example: 'business' no longer means 'busy-ness'

acceptance_tests: derivation distinguished from inflection by criteria

nodes.definition: Assign words to parts of speech using distributional, morphological, and functional criteria rather than meaning alone.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when distributional contexts or morpheme analysis change

pros.claim: distribution gives a language-internal POS test
pros.example: a slot 'the ___ is' selects nouns

cons.claim: category fluidity blurs boundaries
cons.example: 'run' is noun and verb

failure_modes: category assigned by meaning not distribution
acceptance_tests: each label backed by a distributional frame

nodes.definition: Establish which word groups form syntactic constituents using substitution, movement, and coordination tests.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when category labels or diagnostic data change

pros.claim: multiple tests converge on real constituents
pros.example: 'it'-substitution shows an NP

cons.claim: tests can conflict on ambiguous structures
cons.example: a PP attaches ambiguously to V or N

acceptance_tests: each constituent passes at least two tests

nodes.definition: Build phrase-structure rules or X-bar schemas that generate the hierarchical structure of constituents.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when constituency analysis or structural data changes

pros.claim: X-bar captures cross-category structural uniformity
pros.example: NP, VP, PP share head-complement geometry

cons.claim: over-fitting rules to one language loses generality
cons.example: language-specific rules miss universals

acceptance_tests: rules generate attested structures and block unattested ones

nodes.definition: Draw labeled syntactic trees that encode dominance and precedence consistent with phrase-structure rules.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when phrase-structure rules or constituency are revised

pros.claim: trees make dominance and ambiguity visible
pros.example: attachment ambiguity shows as two trees

cons.claim: a tidy tree can mask an unresolved analysis choice
cons.example: drawing forces a binary branch decision

acceptance_tests: tree is licensed by the phrase-structure rules

nodes.definition: Identify subject, object, and other grammatical relations via agreement, case, word order, and voice alternations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when structure or agreement/case evidence changes

pros.claim: relations are testable independent of meaning
pros.example: passive promotes object to subject

cons.claim: relations and thematic roles are easily conflated
cons.example: the subject is not always the agent

failure_modes: thematic role labeled as grammatical relation
relation read off word order alone
acceptance_tests: each relation has a syntactic diagnostic
relation kept distinct from thematic role

nodes.definition: Diagnose structural ambiguity by deriving the distinct trees a string supports and the readings each licenses.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when trees or rules are revised, or a new reading is found

pros.claim: multiple trees expose distinct readings
pros.example: 'old men and women' has two scopes of 'old'

cons.claim: structural and lexical ambiguity are easy to confuse
cons.example: 'bank' ambiguity is lexical, not structural

acceptance_tests: each reading paired with a distinct tree
lexical ambiguity excluded as out of scope

nodes.definition: Test an analysis against cross-linguistic typology and proposed universals to flag typologically anomalous claims.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the analysis or typological baseline changes

pros.claim: typology catches implausible analyses early
pros.example: a claimed OSV-only language violates a universal

cons.claim: universals have exceptions; over-trusting them distorts data
cons.example: a rare type may be genuine, not an error

failure_modes: genuine rare type rejected as error
acceptance_tests: analysis compared to a typological baseline
anomalies flagged with the relevant universal

nodes.definition: Decompose word meaning into sense relations such as synonymy, antonymy, hyponymy, and semantic features.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when usage contexts or category analysis change

pros.claim: sense relations structure the lexicon systematically
pros.example: 'dog' is a hyponym of 'animal'

cons.claim: feature decomposition is hard to bound objectively
cons.example: which features define 'chair' is contestable

acceptance_tests: each sense relation has a substitution or entailment test

nodes.definition: Derive sentence meaning compositionally from the meanings of parts and the syntactic structure combining them.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the syntactic tree or lexical meanings are revised

pros.claim: compositionality explains unbounded sentence meanings
pros.example: meaning tracks the tree, not just the words

cons.claim: idioms and coercion break strict composition
cons.example: 'kick the bucket' is non-compositional

failure_modes: scope read off words not structure
acceptance_tests: meaning derivation mirrors the syntactic tree

nodes.definition: Distinguish the sense of an expression from its reference, and analyze how reference is fixed across contexts.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when context or compositional meaning changes

pros.claim: sense/reference split resolves identity puzzles
pros.example: 'morning star'='evening star' differ in sense

cons.claim: reference depends on context the sentence underdetermines
cons.example: 'I' refers only given a speaker

acceptance_tests: context required for indexical reference is stated

nodes.definition: Verify that phonological, morphological, syntactic, and semantic analyses of the same data are mutually consistent.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when any contributing module analysis changes

pros.claim: cross-module checks catch contradictions one module hides
pros.example: a morpheme boundary must match the phonological one

cons.claim: forcing consistency can paper over a real module mismatch
cons.example: an interface mismatch may be a genuine finding

acceptance_tests: module boundaries align on shared data

nodes.definition: Measure acoustic correlates of speech such as formants, duration, pitch, and voice onset time to ground phonetic claims.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new audio or a revised measurement protocol arrives

pros.claim: acoustic measures make transcription claims checkable
pros.example: VOT separates a voiced from a voiceless stop

cons.claim: acoustic detail can outrun what is linguistically contrastive
cons.example: two formant values may map to one phoneme

failure_modes: instrument artifact read as a cue
acceptance_tests: each cue measured with a stated protocol
measurement kept distinct from contrast claims

nodes.definition: Collect and curate primary language data via elicitation or corpus sampling with documented provenance.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new data sources or elicitation protocols are introduced

pros.claim: documented data lets every later analysis be re-checked
pros.example: glossed elicitation records the source utterance

cons.claim: elicitation bias shapes what is found
cons.example: leading prompts can manufacture a pattern

acceptance_tests: each datum has a documented source
elicitation prompts recorded to expose bias

nodes.definition: Package the full analysis with data, glosses, rules, trees, and decision records into a reproducible handoff artifact.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when any upstream analysis or the consistency report changes

pros.claim: a documented package lets others reproduce the analysis
pros.example: interlinear glosses make each claim checkable

cons.claim: premature packaging locks in unresolved choices
cons.example: freezing a contested tree hides the dispute

acceptance_tests: package reproduces every claim from the data

edges.why_related: contrast analysis operates on the transcribed segments
edges.risk_of_conflict: abstracting before transcription invents contrasts
edges.example: transcribe before testing minimal pairs

edges.why_related: rules derive allophones from the established phonemes
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a fixed inventory anchors rule writing
edges.risk_of_conflict: rules without an inventory have no underlying forms
edges.example: set the inventory before writing rules

edges.why_related: prosodic analysis builds on the transcribed string and its marks
edges.risk_of_conflict: prosody without transcription floats free
edges.example: mark stress on the transcription

edges.why_related: acoustic measurement targets segments fixed by transcription
edges.risk_of_conflict: measuring without a transcription lacks segment anchors
edges.example: label the segment before measuring its VOT

edges.why_related: morpheme cutting compares phonemically analyzed forms
edges.benefit_of_coupling: phoneme analysis stabilizes the forms compared
edges.risk_of_conflict: cutting raw phones confuses allophony with morphology
edges.example: analyze phonemes before cutting morphemes

edges.why_related: paradigm tabulation arranges segmented morphemes by feature
edges.benefit_of_coupling: clean cuts make paradigm cells well defined
edges.risk_of_conflict: tabulating unsegmented words hides the morphemes
edges.example: segment morphemes before tabulating paradigms

edges.why_related: word-formation rules combine segmented morphemes
edges.risk_of_conflict: deriving from unsegmented forms misattributes structure
edges.example: segment before stating derivation rules

edges.why_related: morphological criteria help assign categories
edges.risk_of_conflict: assigning categories without morphology relies on meaning
edges.example: use affix evidence for categories

edges.why_related: constituency tests presuppose category labels
edges.benefit_of_coupling: labeled words make substitution tests meaningful
edges.risk_of_conflict: testing constituents without categories is unanchored
edges.example: label categories before constituency tests

edges.why_related: phrase-structure rules generalize the tested constituents
edges.risk_of_conflict: rules without constituency evidence overgenerate
edges.example: test constituents before writing rules

edges.why_related: trees instantiate the phrase-structure rules
edges.risk_of_conflict: drawing trees without rules invents structure
edges.example: write rules before drawing trees

edges.why_related: relation diagnostics operate over identified constituents
edges.risk_of_conflict: relations read off order without constituents misfire
edges.example: fix constituents before relations

edges.why_related: ambiguity is diagnosed by deriving distinct trees
edges.risk_of_conflict: claiming ambiguity without trees is unsupported
edges.example: derive trees before asserting ambiguity

edges.why_related: the typology check evaluates the structural analysis
edges.benefit_of_coupling: structure provides the object to compare typologically
edges.risk_of_conflict: typology check without an analysis has nothing to test
edges.example: analyze structure before typology check

edges.why_related: relation patterns feed word-order and alignment typology
edges.benefit_of_coupling: relations let alignment type be classified
edges.risk_of_conflict: typology of alignment needs relation evidence
edges.example: establish relations before alignment typology

edges.why_related: sense relations are organized within categories
edges.benefit_of_coupling: category fixes the comparison set for senses
edges.risk_of_conflict: comparing senses across categories conflates types
edges.example: fix category before sense relations

edges.why_related: compositional meaning is computed over the syntactic tree
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the tree supplies the combination order
edges.risk_of_conflict: composing meaning without structure mis-scopes operators
edges.example: build the tree before composing meaning

edges.why_related: composition needs the meanings of the parts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: lexical meanings are the inputs to composition
edges.risk_of_conflict: composing undefined word meanings is empty
edges.example: analyze lexical meaning before composition

edges.why_related: reference analysis builds on the composed sentence meaning
edges.benefit_of_coupling: composition fixes sense before reference is set
edges.risk_of_conflict: fixing reference without sense skips a level
edges.example: compose meaning before reference analysis

edges.why_related: the consistency check consumes the phonological analysis
edges.benefit_of_coupling: phonology supplies one module to reconcile
edges.risk_of_conflict: checking consistency without phonology is incomplete
edges.example: finish phonology before the interface check

edges.why_related: the check reconciles morphology with other modules
edges.risk_of_conflict: interface check missing morphology is partial
edges.example: finish morphology before the interface check

edges.why_related: the check reconciles syntax with semantics and morphology
edges.risk_of_conflict: interface check missing syntax is partial
edges.example: finish syntax before the interface check

edges.why_related: the check reconciles semantics with syntax and morphology
edges.benefit_of_coupling: semantics supplies meaning to align with structure
edges.risk_of_conflict: interface check missing semantics is partial
edges.example: finish semantics before the interface check

edges.why_related: documentation packages the reconciled analysis
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a passed consistency check is a precondition to freeze
edges.risk_of_conflict: documenting an inconsistent analysis ships contradictions
edges.example: reconcile before documenting

edges.why_related: transcription works on the collected primary data
edges.risk_of_conflict: transcribing undocumented data loses provenance
edges.example: collect data before transcribing

edges.why_related: data provenance quality changes the reproducibility of the handoff
edges.risk_of_conflict: weak provenance degrades every documented claim
edges.example: missing source notes make a claim unverifiable

edges.why_related: phonological alternations change which morpheme cut looks right
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating a phonological alternation as a morpheme boundary mis-cuts
edges.example: final devoicing makes one morpheme look like two
edges.resolution_rule: attribute alternation to phonology before positing a morpheme

edges.why_related: a typological anomaly can trigger revisiting the structural analysis
edges.risk_of_conflict: endless re-analysis if every rare type forces revision
edges.example: an OV/VO clash flags a rule to re-examine
edges.resolution_rule: revise structure only if the anomaly survives data re-check; stop after one revision cycle

edges.why_related: a detected interface mismatch can send syntax back for revision
edges.risk_of_conflict: ping-pong revision if both sides keep changing
edges.example: a semantics-syntax clash on subjecthood reopens relations
edges.resolution_rule: revise the module with weaker evidence; stop when consistency holds

edges.why_related: an interface mismatch can send semantics back for revision
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded re-derivation if structure also keeps moving
edges.example: a scope mismatch reopens the meaning derivation
edges.resolution_rule: revise the side with weaker evidence; cap at one cycle per data set

edges.why_related: narrow phonetic detail competes with phonemic abstraction
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balancing keeps both record and analysis honest
edges.risk_of_conflict: too much detail buries contrast; too little hides allophony
edges.example: coding every coarticulation obscures the phoneme
edges.resolution_rule: use narrow transcription as record, broad for contrast

edges.why_related: distributional category criteria pull against meaning-based intuition
edges.risk_of_conflict: defining category by meaning makes the semantic test circular
edges.example: calling 'the rich' a noun by distribution, not meaning
edges.resolution_rule: distribution decides category; meaning informs semantics

edges.why_related: syntactic subjecthood competes with semantic agenthood
edges.risk_of_conflict: equating subject with agent breaks on passives and unaccusatives
edges.example: 'the door' is subject but not agent in 'the door opened'
edges.resolution_rule: grammatical relation is syntactic; thematic role is semantic

edges.why_related: the inflection/derivation boundary creates classification tension
edges.risk_of_conflict: a process on the borderline gets double-counted
edges.example: participles sit between inflection and derivation
edges.resolution_rule: apply the inflection-vs-derivation criteria, record borderline cases

edges.why_related: available data bounds which contrasts are decidable
edges.risk_of_conflict: claiming contrasts beyond the data overreaches
edges.example: a gap in minimal pairs caps what can be proven
edges.resolution_rule: limit inventory claims to what the data supports

edges.why_related: reference analysis should be in place before the interface check
edges.risk_of_conflict: checking interfaces before reference leaves semantics open
edges.example: unresolved deixis blocks a clean semantic module
edges.resolution_rule: finish reference before the consistency check

edges.why_related: both are morphological processes over morphemes
edges.benefit_of_coupling: grouping aids shared tooling and deduplication
edges.risk_of_conflict: blurring them loses the inflection/derivation distinction
edges.example: both attach affixes to a base
edges.resolution_rule: treat as related but keep the functional split

edges.why_related: both concern meaning at and below the word level
edges.risk_of_conflict: merging sense relations with reference loses the sense/reference split
edges.example: both analyze 'meaning' of expressions
edges.resolution_rule: keep sense relations and reference theory distinct

edges.why_related: the check reconciles prosody with segmental and syntactic analysis
edges.benefit_of_coupling: prosody supplies suprasegmental structure to align
edges.risk_of_conflict: an interface check ignoring prosody misses focus effects
edges.example: prosodic phrasing must match syntactic phrasing
edges.resolution_rule: include prosody in the consistency check

edges.why_related: resolving structural ambiguity changes which meaning is composed
edges.risk_of_conflict: composing over the wrong tree yields the wrong meaning
edges.example: picking one attachment fixes the truth conditions
edges.resolution_rule: resolve structural ambiguity before fixing meaning

conflict_axes.trigger: coding all phonetic detail competes with isolating meaning-bearing contrast
resolution_order: abstract to contrastive phonemes for analysis
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: phonetic detail is the record; phonemic contrast governs the analysis
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a phonetic difference is claimed contrastive without a minimal pair or distributional argument
conflict_axes.example: treating an aspirated allophone as a separate phoneme

conflict_axes.trigger: assigning a part of speech by distribution conflicts with assigning it by meaning
resolution_order: use meaning only as a heuristic, not a criterion
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: distribution decides lexical category; meaning informs semantics, not category
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a category is assigned solely because of what a word means
conflict_axes.example: labeling 'the poor' a noun on distribution though it 'means' a property

conflict_axes.trigger: syntactic subjecthood competes with semantic agenthood
resolution_order: fix grammatical relation by syntactic diagnostics
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: grammatical relation is syntactic; thematic role is semantic; never equate them
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a subject is automatically labeled agent or vice versa
conflict_axes.example: 'the window' is subject but patient in 'the window broke'

conflict_axes.trigger: borderline morphology can be classed as either inflection or derivation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: apply the inflection-vs-derivation criteria; flag borderline processes rather than forcing a side
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a process meets criteria for both classes
conflict_axes.example: participle formation sitting between the two classes

conflict_axes.trigger: strict compositionality competes with idioms and context-bound meaning
resolution_order: compose meaning from structure where possible
mark idioms and coercion as exceptions
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: composition is the default; non-compositional cases are flagged exceptions, not silently fitted
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a non-compositional idiom is forced into a compositional derivation
conflict_axes.example: deriving 'kick the bucket' compositionally as literal

conflict_axes.trigger: an elegant language-specific analysis can clash with typological norms
resolution_order: revise only if the anomaly survives data re-check
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: typology flags anomalies but does not override decisive language-internal data
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if an analysis is rejected only for being typologically rare despite strong data
conflict_axes.example: discarding a real OSV pattern because it is cross-linguistically uncommon

conflict_axes.trigger: internally optimal module analyses can be mutually inconsistent
resolution_order: complete each module on its own evidence
revise the module with weaker evidence on mismatch
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: interface consistency governs; the module with weaker internal evidence yields
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if two modules give incompatible boundaries on the same data
conflict_axes.example: a morphological boundary that no phonological rule respects

conflict_axes.trigger: pushing analytic depth competes with keeping every claim documented and reproducible
resolution_order: analyze to the depth the data supports
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reproducibility governs the handoff; undocumented depth is downgraded or flagged
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if an analytic claim cannot be traced to documented data
conflict_axes.example: an elegant rule with no attested form supporting it

edge_cases.trigger: predictable allophones are treated as separate phonemes
edge_cases.example: splitting aspirated and unaspirated [p] into two phonemes in English
edge_cases.detection_method: check each candidate phoneme for a minimal pair or complementary distribution
resolution: merge complementary allophones under one phoneme

edge_cases.trigger: a phonological alternation is read as a morpheme boundary
edge_cases.example: treating final-devoicing variation as two morphemes
edge_cases.detection_method: attribute alternations to phonological rules before positing a boundary
resolution: reassign the alternation to a phonological rule

edge_cases.trigger: category assigned from meaning not distribution
edge_cases.example: calling an event noun a verb because it 'denotes an action'
edge_cases.detection_method: require a distributional frame for every category label

edge_cases.trigger: grammatical relation equated with thematic role
edge_cases.example: labeling the subject of 'the door opened' an agent
edge_cases.detection_method: check each relation against a syntactic diagnostic independent of meaning

edge_cases.trigger: a non-constituent is built into the rules
edge_cases.example: treating 'V NP' plus a stray word as one constituent

edge_cases.trigger: a drawn tree is not licensed by the rules
edge_cases.failure_mode: schema drift between rules and trees
edge_cases.example: a tree branch with no corresponding phrase-structure rule
edge_cases.detection_method: verify each tree node against the rule set
resolution: correct the tree or add the licensing rule

edge_cases.example: drawing one tree for 'I saw the man with the telescope'
edge_cases.detection_method: derive all trees a string supports before fixing one
resolution: add the missing tree and reading
map each reading to a tree

edge_cases.trigger: a rare but real pattern is rejected for being atypical
edge_cases.failure_mode: data discarded to fit a universal
edge_cases.example: rejecting attested object-initial order as an error
edge_cases.detection_method: weigh decisive language-internal data against the universal

edge_cases.trigger: an idiom is forced into compositional derivation
edge_cases.example: deriving 'spill the beans' as literal spilling
edge_cases.detection_method: flag known idioms and coercion before composing

edge_cases.trigger: a cross-module contradiction is silently reconciled
edge_cases.example: forcing a semantic boundary to match an unmotivated syntactic one
edge_cases.detection_method: log every reconciliation and require evidence for the chosen side

edge_cases.trigger: a claim cannot be traced to documented data
edge_cases.example: a rule with no example utterance recorded
edge_cases.detection_method: require a documented source for each datum used

edge_cases.trigger: a contested analysis is frozen before the consistency check passes
edge_cases.example: publishing a tree still disputed across modules
edge_cases.detection_method: block hard lock until the interface check and review pass

workflow.objective: collect and document primary language data
workflow.do_first_because: every later analysis must be reproducible from documented data

workflow.objective: transcribe and measure the speech signal
workflow.do_first_because: nothing phonological is valid without a stable phonetic record

acceptance_tests: each phoneme has a minimal pair or distribution argument
workflow.do_first_because: phonemes and rules underlie morpheme analysis

workflow.objective: segment morphemes and analyze inflection and derivation
acceptance_tests: each cut recurs with stable meaning
inflection separated from derivation by criteria
each label backed by a distributional frame

workflow.do_first_because: structure is the input to relations and semantics

workflow.objective: analyze relations, ambiguity, and typological fit
workflow.do_first_because: relations and ambiguity must be fixed before meaning is composed

workflow.objective: analyze lexical, compositional, and referential meaning
workflow.do_first_because: meaning depends on the locked structure

workflow.objective: reconcile all modules on the shared data
workflow.do_first_because: no artifact may be frozen while modules contradict each other

workflow.objective: package the reproducible analysis for handoff
exit_criteria: analysis documented and ready to hand off
workflow.do_first_because: hand off only a consistent, reviewed, reproducible analysis

priority_rationale.notes: root data source all analysis depends on
categories gate syntax and lexical semantics
selects the right structure to interpret
composed meaning feeds reference and interface

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk analysis decision could be made quickly without checks
dominance_rules.rule: risk-if-wrong dominates speed; high-risk nodes require acceptance tests and human review
dominance_rules.required_action: run acceptance tests and human review before finalizing high-risk nodes
dominance_rules.example: skipping the contrast test to publish an inventory faster

dominance_rules.trigger: a valuable node is tempting to do before its prerequisite
dominance_rules.example: analyzing meaning before the syntactic tree exists

dominance_rules.trigger: a category could be assigned by meaning
dominance_rules.rule: distributional evidence dominates meaning-based intuition for category assignment
dominance_rules.example: calling a word a noun because it 'names a thing'

dominance_rules.trigger: subject and agent are about to be merged
dominance_rules.rule: syntactic relation and semantic role are kept distinct; neither overrides the other's diagnostics
dominance_rules.required_action: label relation and role with separate diagnostics
dominance_rules.example: equating subject with agent on a passive

dominance_rules.trigger: decisive language-internal data conflicts with a universal
dominance_rules.rule: decisive language-internal data dominates a typological universal
dominance_rules.required_action: keep the data-supported analysis, record the anomaly
dominance_rules.example: discarding attested data to satisfy a universal

dominance_rules.rule: interface consistency dominates; the weaker-evidence module yields
dominance_rules.required_action: revise the module with weaker internal evidence
dominance_rules.example: a morphology boundary no phonological rule supports

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number is unsupported by data
dominance_rules.rule: evidence-label correctness dominates numeric precision; unsupported values stay heuristic
dominance_rules.required_action: keep estimates heuristic without observed data
dominance_rules.example: reporting a contrast frequency as if measured

dominance_rules.trigger: an artifact could be locked before tests pass
dominance_rules.rule: QA dominates locking; no hard lock before acceptance and consistency gates pass
dominance_rules.required_action: pass all gates before hard lock
dominance_rules.example: freezing a tree before the consistency check

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or contested call is about to be automated
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for high-risk and contested analyses
dominance_rules.required_action: route high-risk nodes to human review
dominance_rules.example: auto-accepting a disputed fallacy of segmentation

dominance_rules.trigger: an analytic claim outruns documented data
dominance_rules.rule: reproducibility dominates analytic depth; undocumented claims are downgraded
dominance_rules.required_action: ground every claim in documented data before deepening
dominance_rules.example: an elegant rule with no attested supporting form

anti_rework_rules.rule: document primary data before analyzing it
anti_rework_rules.rationale: analyzing undocumented data forces re-collection later
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a claim with no traceable source
anti_rework_rules.example: transcribing a clip whose origin is unrecorded

anti_rework_rules.rationale: abstracting before transcription invents or misses contrasts
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: contrast claims revised when transcription changes
anti_rework_rules.example: testing minimal pairs on an unstable transcription

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the phoneme inventory before writing rules
anti_rework_rules.rationale: rules over an unstable inventory get rewritten
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: rules edited after every inventory change
anti_rework_rules.example: ordering rules before the underlying forms are set

anti_rework_rules.rationale: paradigms built on bad cuts must be rebuilt
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: paradigm cells re-cut after segmentation changes

anti_rework_rules.rationale: constituency tests without categories are unanchored
anti_rework_rules.example: running substitution tests on unlabeled words

anti_rework_rules.rule: verify constituents before writing phrase-structure rules
anti_rework_rules.example: positing rules for an untested word group

anti_rework_rules.rationale: trees not licensed by rules must be redrawn
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a tree branch with no rule
anti_rework_rules.example: drawing a tree then inventing a rule for it

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix syntactic structure before composing meaning
anti_rework_rules.rationale: meaning composed over the wrong tree is wrong
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: meaning re-derived after the tree changes
anti_rework_rules.example: scoping a quantifier before the tree is fixed

anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a handoff package with internal contradictions
anti_rework_rules.example: freezing analyses that disagree across modules

anti_rework_rules.rule: pass acceptance and review gates before hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: premature hard lock forces a version increment to undo
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a hard-locked node that later fails a gate
anti_rework_rules.example: locking a tree before the consistency gate passes

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and downstream coupling
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix may affect downstream nodes
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents of the changed node

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is selected for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to its repair subsystem
action: route the defect to its owner subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator on the affected scope

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or a metric change occurs
action: recompute derived fields with the formula script

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or contested defect cannot be auto-repaired

iteration_protocol.detection: check remaining defects against the materiality threshold
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: all remaining defects are below threshold

checks.expected: each major node maps a CQ

test_cases.input_summary: a word list needing minimal-pair analysis
expected_properties: each phoneme has a minimal pair or distribution argument
phonological alternation not cut as a morpheme
each reading mapped to a distinct tree

test_cases.input_summary: a data set analyzed across all modules

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked analysis change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
